source_model: uniform circular Lambertian emitter; paraxial geometric propagation
retinal_coverage_definition: source-pupil footprint covers the specified posterior-pole disk at the fixed retina plane
assumptions: The effective eye is represented by a rotationally symmetric paraxial thin lens.
Each eye is evaluated only at three fixed air-equivalent focal lengths; no continuous accommodation or focal-length fitting is used in the requested sweep.
The three fixed focal lengths are the PPT range endpoints plus their arithmetic midpoint: chick 7.5/8.0/8.5 mm, child 13.5/15.1/16.7 mm, adult 12.8/14.75/16.7 mm.
The fixed retina plane uses the reported axial length divided by an image-medium refractive index of 1.336 in the reduced-angle ABCD translation.

For every object distance, pupil diameter, and fixed focal length, the model reports both the geometric minimum source size and a conservative source size whose full-overlap plateau covers the posterior-pole disk.
The source is spatially uniform and circular; absolute radiometric power and tissue safety are out of scope because the PPT supplies no source flux or exposure time.
External-lens vertex distances are provisional: 5 mm for chick and 12 mm for human eyes; external-lens combinations are deferred until the corrected fixed-focal baseline is accepted.
